part_1_frame_authority_ruling.question_raised_by_operator: The frozen design's authoritative frame appears to be available_time over three sources at 4,048 rows, while the reviewer's accepted cost figure of 4,727 corresponds to published_at over two sources. These are different sets.
part_1_frame_authority_ruling.ruling: The operator is correct. The authoritative candidate frame is available_time over the three audited sources, 4,048 rows for 2026-08-06 through 08-08 Shanghai.

evidence.shipped_code_is_decisive: scripts/build_p4_2a_gold_sample.py, _heldout_candidate_rows, filters on start <= row.available_time < end. This is the byte-frozen code path both v1.7 and v2 use; the question is settled by what the selector actually does, not by prose.
evidence.v1_7_reproduction: Recomputing the v1.7 window 2026-08-04 to 08-05 with available_time over the three audited sources yields cninfo 1,982 plus akshare_ths 875 plus sina 213 equals exactly 3,070, which reproduces the recorded raw candidate count for that round precisely. No other framing reproduces it.

set_difference.note: the two sets genuinely differ; this was not a rounding or counting slip

part_1_frame_authority_ruling.why_available_time_is_also_semantically_: available_time is the point-in-time ingestion instant and is never backfilled. It defines what the system actually knew and when, which is the population an extractor operating in production would see. published_at would silently pull in items that only reached the database later through the backlog migration, which the system did not have at the time.

my_error.statement: The 4,727 figure I accepted was computed on the wrong field and the wrong source set: published_at rather than available_time, and two sources rather than three. It was not a conservative reading of the design; it was a different query.
my_error.pattern: This is the third cost or volume figure I have had to correct in two days, after C-1 and C-3, and all three ran in the same direction. The rule I set for myself in C-3, derive figures from measured pool sizes, was not sufficient: the measurement must also use the field the shipped selector uses. Any future frame size I quote must be produced by the selector's own predicate, not by a hand-written query.

part_1_frame_authority_ruling.disposition_of_4727: It stands only as a conservative upper bound on the cost already accepted. The accepted ceiling is not reduced by this ruling, so no new cost acceptance is required, but the realised figures will be lower.

part_2_design_ambiguity_finding.statement: The frozen v2 design's heldout_frame_v2.source_window declares only a timezone and start and end instants. Neither available_time nor published_at appears anywhere in config/p4_event_evaluation_v2.yaml. The authoritative field is therefore recoverable only by reading the selector implementation.
part_2_design_ambiguity_finding.why_this_matters: A pre-registered frame whose population cannot be determined from the pre-registration itself is under-specified. Two competent parties read it differently within one day, which is the practical demonstration.
part_2_design_ambiguity_finding.disposition_now: Do NOT amend config/p4_event_evaluation_v2.yaml. Its SHA 18a2428a is bound to the sealed development frame, the dev45 gold and three recorded calibration rounds. Changing its bytes to fix prose would break those bindings for no evaluative gain. This record is the authoritative interpretation instead, and must be cited by the heldout round evidence.
part_2_design_ambiguity_finding.required_in_future_designs: Any future evaluation design must name the timestamp field and the exact source set in the window declaration, so the population is determinable from the pre-registration without reading code.
